title: Finite purely inseparable extensions test geometric reducedness of any algebra
statement: Let $k$ be a field and $C$ a commutative $k$-algebra. Tensor products carry their usual algebra multiplication [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. The following are equivalent: (1) for every finite purely inseparable field extension $E/k$ [def-pc-field-extension, def-weil-pbc-finite-purely-inseparable-extension], including $E=k$, the ring $C\otimes_kE$ is reduced; (2) for every field extension $K/k$, the ring $C\otimes_kK$ is reduced. Here reduced means that $x^n=0$ for $n\ge1$ implies $x=0$. No finite generation, Noetherianity, or reducedness hypothesis on $C$ is imposed, and the zero algebra is allowed.

source.place: Tag 030V, lemma-geometrically-reduced-finite-purely-inseparable-extension, equivalence (1) and (5), with the definition of geometrically reduced expanded.
